newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hansapank says Latvia unit made loss.
newsitem.headline: Hansapank says Latvia unit made loss.

text.p: The largest bank in the Baltic states, Estonia's Hansapank, on Monday gave revised figures for its Latvian subsidiary Hansabank Latvija and said the new figure showed a loss rather than a profit for the first nine months.

It said in a statement that the central bank of Latvia audited Hansabank Latvija after which it decided to increase the provision for credit losses by 13.55 million kroons, putting the Latvian unit into a 12.46 million kroon loss after nine months.
Hansapank, which made a total group profit of 169 million kroons in the first nine months, had previously said the Latvian subsidiary made a profit of 1.3 million kroons.
But Hansapank added that most of the loans have already been repaid and that the provision for credit losses would decrease at the end of the year.
Hansapank bought the Latvian bank, formerly called Deutsche Lettische Bank, in June, making it the first cross-border bank merger in the Baltic states.
Hansapank has a stock market quote in Tallinn and Helsinki.
